title: The contribution of religion

draft.title: The contribution of religion
card: Religion can give an individual a sense of meaning. It offers answers to questions such as why we are here and what happens after death.
Religion can give a sense of identity, a feeling of belonging to a faith and its story. It can also give guidance, as its ethics and teachings help a person decide how to act.
For a society, religion can supply shared values, such as care for others, that many people hold in common. It can also build community, as people gather to worship and support one another.
Religion can also mark life's stages, such as birth, coming of age, marriage and death, with ceremonies that the community shares.
draft.remember: Religion can serve a person with meaning, identity and guidance, and a society with values, community and ceremonies.

a.q: Which example shows religion giving guidance to an individual?
opts: A teenager uses her faith's ethics to decide whether to lie
A town holds a yearly festival for all its residents
A family holds a naming ceremony for a newborn baby
A man feels he belongs to a global faith community
a.why: Guidance means teachings or ethics that help a person decide how to act, and the teenager uses them to make a choice. The festival shows community, and the naming ceremony marks a life stage. Feeling that he belongs is identity, which is the most tempting wrong option because it also affects one person.
a.clue: Look for the person using teachings to choose how to act.

b.q: A mosque in Lakemba holds a wedding for two members, and many of the congregation attend and help with the feast. Which contribution of religion does the wedding show most directly?
opts: Marking a life stage, with the community taking part
Giving an individual meaning about life after death
Giving guidance through ethics on how to act
Giving a person an identity that is separate from society
b.why: A wedding is a ceremony that marks a stage of life, and the congregation shares in it. Meaning about death and ethical guidance are not what this event shows. Identity is the tempting wrong option, but the event centres on a shared ceremony and not on how one person sees themselves.
b.clue: Think about what kind of event a wedding is in a person's life.

a.best: A teenager uses her faith's ethics to decide whether to lie

b.best: Marking a life stage, with the community taking part
